chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no Zakat regarding the wealth of the contracted slave.
ai.seo_question: Is Zakat due on the wealth of a Mukatab (contracted slave) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing that a Mukatab’s wealth is exempt from Zakat to facilitate their gradual emancipation. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic view that the Mukatab’s assets are earmarked for fulfilling their contract with the master, thereby prioritizing their social and economic liberation over obligatory almsgiving.
